title: 5 Best Commodities to Trade in India (2026), Ranked by MCX Futures Turnover
summary: Gold, silver, crude oil, natural gas or copper? See the most traded commodities in India by MCX futures turnover, their lot sizes and who each one suits.

## 5 Best Commodities to Trade in India


### 1. Gold


Gold ranked first by MCX futures turnover. MCX lists it in five sizes, from Gold (1 kg) down to Gold Petal (1 gram), so you can choose how much exposure you take per lot.


-


Prices move with US interest rates, the US dollar, inflation, central bank buying and the rupee.


-


Options trade on Gold and Gold Mini.


**Suits:** Traders who want to match their position size closely to their capital.


### 2. Silver


Silver often swings more sharply than gold, because its demand comes from both investors and industries like solar panels and electronics.


-


Contract sizes are Silver (30 kg), Silver Mini (5 kg), Silver Micro (1 kg) and Silver 100 (100 grams).


-


Options trade on Silver and Silver Mini.


**Suits:** Traders who are comfortable with bigger price swings than gold.


### 3. Crude Oil


Crude oil is the most traded energy contract on MCX. It reacts quickly to OPEC+ decisions, geopolitical news and weekly US inventory data.


-


Contract sizes are Crude Oil (100 barrels) and Crude Oil Mini (10 barrels).


-


The US crude inventory report usually comes out on Wednesdays at 8 PM IST (9 PM after US daylight saving ends), except in holiday weeks.


**Suits:** Traders who can follow the evening session.

### 4. Natural Gas


Natural gas prices can swing sharply within a single session. They are driven by US weather forecasts, LNG exports and weekly storage data.


-


Contract sizes are Natural Gas (1,250 mmBtu) and Natural Gas Mini (250 mmBtu).


-


The US gas storage report usually comes out on Thursdays at 8 PM IST (9 PM after US daylight saving ends), except in holiday weeks.


**Suits:** Experienced traders with strict position sizing and stop-losses.

### 5. Copper


Copper is the most traded base metal on MCX. Its price often tracks global industrial demand, especially from China.


-


The contract size is 2,500 kg, and options trade on Copper.


-


Prices also follow London Metal Exchange (LME) prices and global manufacturing data.


**Suits:** Traders who follow global economic trends.


#### Other Commodities


Aluminium, zinc, lead and nickel also trade on MCX, along with cotton, mentha oil, cardamom and electricity. Agri commodities like guar seed, jeera and turmeric trade mainly on NCDEX. These contracts usually see far less turnover, so read our guide to[liquidity in trading](https://algotest.in/blog/what-is-liquidity-in-trading/) before you trade them.

### FAQs


#### Which is the best commodity to trade in India?


There is no single best commodity for everyone. Gold, silver, crude oil, natural gas and copper were the five most traded on MCX by futures turnover in April to June 2026, so most traders choose among them based on capital and trading hours.


#### What is the most traded commodity in India?


Gold ranked first by MCX futures turnover in April to June 2026, with a 34.5% share. Silver was second at 29.7%, and crude oil was third at 16.6%.


#### Which commodity is best for intraday trading?


Traders often choose crude oil, natural gas, gold or silver for intraday trading because these contracts see heavy turnover on MCX. Check the spread and depth of your exact contract, and your broker’s intraday square-off time, before you trade.


#### Which commodity is best for beginners?


Many beginners start with smaller contracts like Gold Petal, Gold Ten, Silver 100 or Crude Oil Mini to keep exposure per lot low. A smaller lot does not make the market easier, so learn how margin, expiry and delivery work first.


#### How much money do I need to trade commodities in India?


It depends on how you trade. Futures need margin set by the exchange and your broker. Buying an option needs only the premium, while selling an option needs margin, which is usually much higher than the premium.
